o1.biggest_strength: It does the hard thinking the data demands: ranks channels by retained users with the math, treats the 58% migration problem as the central risk, waves the rollout with a stop rule, and gates launch on carry-over tests before the code freeze.
o1.biggest_mistake: Voice slips in a couple of places: 'Bad news to fix first' reads slightly off-brand, and the X post is thinner than the email; the launch-day post could carry a bit more of the craft and community warmth the email shows.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten voice consistency across the X post and plan copy, add a named community-credit moment on launch day (an author roll call), and put the X post's 'press ⌥ Space and watch' next to an explicit 'will my hotkeys work' line in the first post rather than only in the email.

o2.biggest_strength: Voice and craft are excellent: the email and the five-part X thread sound like Raycast, credit authors by name, show the shortcut, and directly answer the 'will my setup move' fear; the multi-post X structure with recordings matches the 'show it moving' principle.
o2.biggest_mistake: It spreads launch across too many days and channels and asks for more simultaneous work than a small team can do: Show HN and full email and creators and authors all at 16:00 on 8 Dec, Product Hunt on 9 Dec, four-plus X posts, plus a 1,000-person beta, daily engineering support shifts, and a claims list — it's ambitious for one launch manager, one designer, one editor and 3 support staff, and some gates (1,000 beta users, zero losses) are stricter than the team can realistically prove by 4 Dec.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut scope to what the team can actually run: fewer dated commitments, a simpler staged-rollout gate, a realistic beta size, and consolidate the launch-day surface so the small team can execute it flawlessly.

reason: Both are strong and both get the data right, but output 1 is the one I'd actually run: it makes the migration gate and staged rollout the spine of the plan and keeps scope inside our four-person team, while output 2 has the better voice and X thread but asks for more than we can deliver on launch day.
